description: We are Last Seen. We tell the stories of the machines humanity left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. From silent rovers to probes still traveling beyond Earth, we turn NASA’s hardware, science, and discoveries into inspiring stories for the next generation of space explorers. Some missions end. Their stories don’t.
summary:
We spent our time coming together to decide our topic and brainstorm our ideas for the story. During this time we discussed the characters, decided what their planet should look like, and what our main problem could be. After these discussions, a captivating story and a comic book was born.
Our story begins when characters Rhea, Wyndex, and Xylos face a natural phenomenon we call "global cooling" on a distant and very different planet, it follows their adventure as they try to find a solution to this problem. The main topic written in the story is global cooling. Why we chose global cooling; is that on Earth, our home, we are facing a problem that is similar in a way, yet also the exact opposite in other perspectives. Through this contrast, we aimed to influence and educate middle school students with a captivating comic book plot, which alien characters solve the problem their planet face with help of the "Artemis Project” they soon discover. It was very special to us and we enjoyed it a lot. We hope you enjoy it as well. Happy reading!
details: Our main goal is to educate our target audience, middle school students and the younger generation, about the threat of global warming, space debris left behind, and the fact that this debris can also be considered cultural heritage, through fun methods such as the comic book we created. Through educating the next generation we plan to be able to raise a generation with better knowledge and an informed society who will work to take precautions for the possible severe effects of global warming. We think our project is creative because we didn't use an experiment or invention to educate but a fun and unique way to achieve that. Our team considered that we must give scientific facts in a way middle school students could understand, so we incorporated data into our compelling plot to make sure it's understandable by the targeted group of readers.
